title: Green Egg Scramble on Buttered Toast

steps.text: Toast the bread and butter it while it is still hot.
Melt a knob more butter in a nonstick pan and wilt the spinach over medium heat, about a minute.
Pour in the eggs, keep the heat low, and draw the curds slowly to the center with a spatula.
When the pan looks nearly dry, pull it off the heat — a food thermometer should read 160 °F in the softest fold.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Fold in the cheddar so it melts into ribbons, then spoon over the toast and eat right away.

title: Tahini Honey Yogurt Bowl with Apple and Toasted Oats

steps.text: Toast the rolled oats in a dry pan over medium heat until they smell nutty, two to three minutes, then tip them out.
Stir the tahini and honey together in the bottom of a wide bowl.
Spoon the greek yogurt over the tahini, then add the apple, sliced thin.
Scatter the warm oats on top and finish with another thread of honey if you like.

title: Ginger Rice Porridge with Egg and Green Onions

steps.text: Bring the chicken stock to a simmer with the ginger, grated straight in.
Add the cooked rice and stir, breaking up clumps, until the grains loosen and the porridge turns creamy, eight to ten minutes.
Season with the soy sauce and check the salt.
Drizzle the beaten eggs slowly over the surface while stirring in circles, and keep stirring until a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Ladle into bowls and shower with the green onions.

title: Lemon Orzo Salad with Cucumber and Feta

steps.text: Cook the orzo in well-salted water, drain it, and spread it on a plate to cool fast.
Dice the cucumber and crumble the feta while the orzo cools.
Whisk the lemon juice with the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Toss everything together, taste for lemon, and pack it up — it only gets better by lunchtime.

title: Smoky Black Bean and Corn Wrap with Lime Yogurt

steps.text: Warm a little oil in a skillet and toast the corn until it picks up dark spots.
Add the black beans with the cumin and smoked paprika, mash a handful against the pan, and let everything thicken for a few minutes.
Stir the lime juice into the greek yogurt with a pinch of salt.
Warm the flour tortillas, then load them with the beans, corn, and cheddar and fold them into wraps.
Serve with the lime yogurt for dipping, or wrap tight for a lunchbox.

title: Lemony Tuna and White-Bean Lettuce Cups

steps.text: Drain the tuna and the white beans well — soggy cups are the only way to ruin this.
Slice the celery thin and toss it with the tuna, beans, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and plenty of black pepper.
Separate the lettuce into cup-shaped leaves and pat them dry.
Spoon the salad into the leaves just before eating so they stay crisp.

title: Garlicky Tomato Spaghetti with Basil

steps.text: Start the dry pasta in well-salted boiling water and pull it a minute shy of the box time.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil with the sliced garlic over medium-low heat until it just turns golden — never brown.
Pour in the canned tomatoes, crush them with your spoon, and simmer hard for ten minutes until the sauce darkens and smells sweet.
Drag the pasta from the pot into the sauce and finish it in the pan with a ladle of the cooking water and toss until every strand is coated.
Tear in the basil, shower with parmesan, and serve.

title: Sesame Chicken Stir-Fry with Broccoli

steps.text: Toss the sliced chicken breast with the cornstarch and half the soy sauce and let it sit while you cut the broccoli into small florets.
Get a wide pan properly hot, add a spoon of neutral-tasting oil, and sear the chicken in one layer without moving it for two minutes.
Flip, add the broccoli and a splash of water, cover, and steam until the florets turn glossy green, about three minutes.
Uncover, add the garlic and the rest of the soy sauce, and toss over high heat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F at the thickest piece.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Finish with the sesame oil and serve over the warm cooked rice.

title: Quick Spinach and Chickpea Coconut Curry

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in oil with a pinch of salt, five minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder and stir until the kitchen smells like a spice box.
Pour in the coconut milk and the drained chickpeas and let the pot burble for five minutes.
Fold in the spinach a handful at a time so it slumps into the sauce.
Taste for salt, spoon over the warm cooked rice, and eat.

title: Red Lentil and Canned-Tomato Soup

steps.text: Sweat the diced onion and carrot in the olive oil with a pinch of salt until they bend, about eight minutes.
Stir in the cumin, then the canned tomatoes, and let them fry briefly in the oil.
Add the red lentils and vegetable stock, bring to a boil, then simmer until the lentils collapse, twenty minutes or so.
Blend a cup of the soup and stir it back in for body, then season hard and eat with toast.

title: Tomato-Simmered Eggs with Warm Tortillas

steps.text: Fry the diced onion in the olive oil until it takes color at the edges, then add the cumin and canned tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens, ten minutes.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover the pan and cook over low heat until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in an egg — the whites should look firm around it.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the flour tortillas in a dry pan while the eggs finish.
Shower the pan with cheddar and bring it to the table with the tortillas for scooping.

title: Golden Potato and Green Pea Curry with Rice

steps.text: Brown the diced onion in oil, then add the ginger, turmeric, and cumin and fry until the spices turn brick-golden.
Add the cubed potatoes and enough water to half cover, and simmer covered for fifteen minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and the green peas and cook until the sauce thickens and the potatoes yield to a fork.
Salt it well and serve over the warm cooked rice.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon over Garlicky Kale

steps.text: Squeeze half the lemon over the salmon fillets and salt them while the pan heats.
Sear the fillets skin-side down in the olive oil without moving them until the skin crisps and releases, four to five minutes.
Flip, cook two minutes more, and check with a food thermometer until it reads 145 °F at the thickest point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: In the same pan, wilt the kale with the garlic and a splash of water until it turns deep green and silky.
Plate the kale under the fish and finish with the rest of the lemon.

title: Lemon-Oregano Chicken Thighs with Yellow Rice

steps.text: Rub the chicken thighs with the oregano, salt, and the juice of one lemon, and let them sit ten minutes.
Sear them skin-side down in the olive oil until the skin turns deep bronze, then turn and add the garlic.
Pour in the chicken stock, cover, and let the thighs braise gently for fifteen minutes.
Check the thickest thigh with a food thermometer until it reads 165 °F before you rest anything on a plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Boil the braising liquid down with the juice of the second lemon and spoon it over the warm cooked rice with the thighs on top.

title: Gochujang Ground Beef Rice Bowls

steps.text: Brown the ground beef hard in a hot pan, breaking it up only now and then so it keeps some crusty edges.
Push the beef aside, melt a little oil in the cleared spot, and fry the garlic and ginger until fragrant, thirty seconds.
Stir in the gochujang and soy sauce and toss everything together with a splash of water to make a glossy sauce.
Keep it frying until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of the pan.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Spoon the beef over bowls of warm cooked rice and finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Creamy Coconut Chana Saag

steps.text: Cook the onion down in oil until it is deep gold — this is where the sweetness comes from, so give it ten minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and garam masala and fry for a minute until aromatic.
Add the canned tomatoes and cook them dry until the oil separates at the edges, then stir in the coconut milk and chickpeas.
Simmer ten minutes so the sauce thickens, then add the spinach in waves and let each wilt before adding more.
Salt to taste and serve over the warm cooked rice.

title: Harissa Roasted Cauliflower with Tahini and Parsley

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425 °F — an oven setting, not a doneness temperature.
Break the cauliflower into big florets and toss with the harissa paste, olive oil, and salt, getting into every crevice.
Roast with the chickpeas on a wide sheet pan until the edges blacken in spots, thirty to thirty-five minutes, turning once.
Stir the tahini together with the lemon juice, loosening with water until the sauce pours off the spoon.
Spread the tahini sauce on a platter, pile the pan on top, and scatter the parsley over everything.

title: Green Curry Tofu with Green Beans

steps.text: Press the tofu between paper towels under a weight while you trim the green beans.
Fry the curry powder and garlic in oil until fragrant, then pour in the coconut milk and bring it to a lazy simmer.
Add the tofu in cubes and the green beans and poach gently until the beans turn bright and the sauce coats a spoon.
Season with the soy sauce and serve over the warm cooked rice.

title: Big-Batch Beef and Black Bean Chili

steps.text: Sear the ground beef in a heavy pot and let it crust before you stir.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper and cook until they soften into the drippings.
Stir in the cumin and smoked paprika, then the canned tomatoes and black beans with their liquid.
Simmer uncovered for forty-five minutes, stirring now and then, until it is thick and brick-dark.
Before the final taste, check the pot with a food thermometer until the beef reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Chill what you do not eat; later, reheat each portion until a food thermometer reads 165 °F all the way through.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Slow Sunday Red Sauce with Rigatoni

steps.text: Warm the olive oil with the crushed garlic in a wide pot until the garlic barely blisters.
Add the canned tomatoes, half a cup of water, and salt, and let it all bubble very slowly for forty minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce turns deep red-orange and drops oil at the edges.
Boil the dry pasta, save a mug of its water, and finish the pasta right in the sauce.
Tear in the basil and serve with the parmesan.
Leftover sauce keeps four days; reheat it until a food thermometer reads 165 °F, loosening with water if it has thickened.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Coconut Red Lentil Dal with Spinach

steps.text: Simmer the red lentils with three cups of water and the turmeric until they fall apart, twenty-five minutes, adding water if they stick.
In a small pan, fry the onion in oil until browned, then add the garlic, ginger, and cumin for one fragrant minute.
Scrape the frying pan into the lentils along with the coconut milk and simmer ten minutes more.
Wilt the spinach into the dal, salt it generously, and serve over the warm cooked rice.
It thickens as it sits; when you bring it back, reheat gently until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Smashed Cucumber Salad with Sesame and Rice Vinegar

steps.text: Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife so they crack, then tear them into rough chunks.
Salt them and let them drain in a colander for five minutes while you grate the garlic.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic together.
Pat the cucumber dry, dress it, and eat cold.

title: Roasted Zucchini with Mint and Feta

steps.text: Cut the zucchini into thick fingers — thin ones shrivel — and toss with the olive oil and salt.
Roast in a hot oven until the undersides caramelize, about fifteen minutes, without stirring more than once.
Crumble the feta over the hot zucchini so it softens at the edges.
Finish with the mint, torn, and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Basil Parmesan White Beans on Toast

steps.text: Warm the sliced garlic in the olive oil until it barely turns blond.
Add the white beans with a splash of their liquid and simmer gently until they thicken their own sauce, eight minutes.
Crush a spoonful of the beans against the pot for creaminess and season well.
Stir in the basil off the heat and serve in bowls with the parmesan over the top.
